Curriculum

What Will You Learn in a CTEC 60 Hour Course?

Qualifying education introduces tax preparation through three required subject areas:

SubjectHoursFocus
Federal tax law43Federal income tax concepts and return preparation
Ethics2Professional responsibilities and ethical conduct
California tax law15California income taxation and state-specific rules
Total60Qualifying education

Subjects covered in CTEC’s curriculum guidelines include filing status, dependents, income, deductions, credits, self-employment, property transactions, retirement income, California adjustments, and professional responsibilities. Schools organize their lessons differently, so review the actual syllabus before selecting a course. See CTEC’s QE curriculum guidelines.

Buying guide

Choosing a Course When You’re New to Tax Preparation

Think about what will help you work through unfamiliar material. A lower price may be attractive, but an accessible explanation or useful support can matter just as much.

For a fuller buying checklist, read how to choose a CTEC tax course.

Teaching format: Decide whether you prefer video explanations, reading, scheduled instruction, or a mixture.
Practice: Check for worked examples and practice questions so you can apply what you learn.
Help when you need it: Look for clear support hours and an explanation of whether an instructor answers tax-content questions.
Study materials: Find out whether downloadable notes or printed materials are included.
Access period: Confirm when the course expires and whether you can review completed lessons.
Assessment policy: Read the passing requirements, retake rules, and any additional charges.
Cost

How Much Does a CTEC 60 Hour Course Cost?

Tuition varies by school and package. Compare the complete course price, including any required materials or fees, and check which upgrades are optional.

Keep course tuition separate from the other costs involved in becoming registered. A course purchase does not automatically include your CTEC application, fingerprinting, registration, PTIN, or tax preparer bond. Confirm any claimed bundle with the provider.

Registration

What Else Do You Need to Become a CTEC Registered Tax Preparer?

Education is one part of registration. CTEC’s new-applicant process also includes an application, fingerprinting and background review, a valid IRS PTIN, a $5,000 tax preparer surety bond, and completion of registration and payment.

CTEC permits applicants to begin the course before the background-review process is complete, but passing the course does not guarantee registration. Follow CTEC’s current new-applicant instructions when planning your next steps.

Questions

CTEC 60 Hour Course Questions

Is the 60-hour course the same as the 20-hour course?

No. The 60-hour course is qualifying education for the entry process. The 20-hour CTEC course is annual continuing education for registered preparers.

Can I take the CTEC 60 hour course online?

Online options are available. Confirm whether the course is self-paced or scheduled, how lessons and exams work, and whether your preferred device is supported.

Do I need tax preparation experience first?

Qualifying education covers foundational material. Check the school’s entry requirements and sample lessons to judge whether its pace and explanations suit your starting knowledge.

Is there an exam?

CTEC’s self-study standards include examination requirements. Ask the provider how assessments are organized, what score is required, and what support or retakes are available. See CTEC’s QE standards.

How long do I have to complete the course?

The school sets its course-access and completion terms. CTEC separately states that completed qualifying education is valid for up to 18 months from completion. Plan both the course and registration around the applicable dates. See CTEC’s new-application timeframes.

Can I prepare tax returns as soon as I finish?

Completing the course alone does not grant CTEC registration. If you are required to register, complete the remaining application and registration requirements before practicing. CTEC explains the process in its new-preparer instructions.

How do I know a provider offers approved qualifying education?

Check the school’s current qualifying education approval in the CTEC provider directory. Approval for continuing education alone is not the same as approval for qualifying education.
